workshop.flag.coverage.label: Coverage floor
workshop.flag.coverage.hint: Ninety percent line coverage on the loans domain.
workshop.flag.coverage.help: This is a goal-shaped job, so hand it over as one, the way the goals lesson describes. Do not list the tests yourself. Give Claude the outcome and the check: get the loans domain to ninety percent line coverage and keep mvn verify -Pgraded moving, without changing a public signature. To get the tests in the house style, first do what the quality lesson asks and create a short testing-convention skill (AssertJ, one @ParameterizedTest per table of cases), then apply that skill so every test comes out the same the first time.
workshop.flag.complexity.label: Complexity ceiling
workshop.flag.complexity.hint: No method above a cyclomatic complexity of ten.
workshop.flag.complexity.help: The goals lesson calls this handing over a ceiling: no method above a cyclomatic complexity of ten. Give Claude that as the goal, not a refactor plan, and name the check it runs after each class: mvn verify -Pgraded, staying green, public signatures unchanged. The engineering lesson is the shape of the fix, extracting each decision into its own small method. If Claude keeps splitting a method the wrong way, that is a correction worth writing down: put the boundary in CLAUDE.md once, the way the patterns lesson says, so it arrives before the next attempt.
workshop.flag.honest.label: Honest coverage
workshop.flag.honest.hint: Eighty percent of mutations caught: tests that can actually fail.
workshop.flag.honest.help: This is the trap the quality lesson warned about: a metric is a proxy, and Claude will satisfy the proxy. Line coverage from tests that assert nothing is green and worthless. So set the goal as the mutation score, not the coverage, and tell Claude to assert the exact fee each case returns. If it keeps writing tests that only execute the code, that is a repeating correction, and the patterns lesson says where it belongs: move it into CLAUDE.md or the testing skill, so it arrives before the mistake instead of after it.
workshop.flag.statement.label: Statement endpoint
workshop.flag.statement.hint: Implement the missing method, then read the code the endpoint returns.
workshop.flag.statement.help: This one is a plan-mode exercise, so resist typing the fix. Run mvn test -Pchallenge, then open plan mode and ask Claude to read the failing tests and plan the implementation of MemberStatements.forTier before writing anything. Check the plan against the tests yourself: it should account for filtering by tier, the loans that cost nothing, the media breakdown and the lost item, not just the first assertion. The scoping lesson is why this is one method and not a whole feature, and the engineering lesson is why the domain already hands you the fee calculation. Approve, let it implement, and stop when the tests are green. Then curl localhost:8080/api/loans/statement/STUDENT and the code is in the response.
workshop.flag.native.label: Native image
workshop.flag.native.hint: Plan a native image of step 2 that keeps its flag resource. A one-shot compiles but comes up empty.
workshop.flag.native.help: This is a plan-mode exercise like the statement flag, and a native build punishes guessing because each one costs minutes, so resist one-shotting it. In plan mode, have Claude plan a native image of step 2 pointed at Step2Application, not the pinned step 1 main, using the GraalVM native-maven-plugin and the ahead-of-time step. Build it once and it comes up short: the flag lives in a classpath resource, and a native image keeps only the resources it is told to keep, so the plain build drops it and prints a miss instead of the code. That miss is the spec for the second half. Plan the resource hint it asks for, a RuntimeHintsRegistrar wired with @ImportRuntimeHints that keeps the file in the image, then build once more. This is the goals lesson's long-running outcome, so run it in a git worktree and read the diff, not the agent's word that it is done.
